data.content_ref: inline:The problem explicitly requires determining 'when resumption must stay refused,' yet SRC_001's main claim asserts resumption is 'always permissible' under a single structural condition and never identifies any case where append-only identity mandates refusal. More critically, the problem demands adjudicating 'between rival criteria wherever the evidence allows.' SRC_001's own counterconditions raise exactly the rival criteria that matter—semantic coherence of the stream vs. structural append-only validity, workflow-contract single-run continuity vs. storage integrity, causal identity including single-run continuity vs. causal chain as linked list—but files them all as bare observations without resolving which criterion governs or under what conditions one dominates another. By asserting one criterion (storage invariant) as definitive in the main claim while noting competing criteria only as unresolved observations, SRC_001 fails the adjudication requirement the problem imposes.
